item.title: Port Slack app is now in open beta
item.description: Port's Slack app lets you ask questions and get immediate answers about your software catalog directly in Slack. You can also trigger workflows like creating a Jira ticket or deploying a service without leaving your conversation.

item.title: Port × n8n Community Session Recap: Boosting AI Workflows with Context and Guardrails
item.description: Automations promised us both speed and control. And in the age of AI, we expect them to outperform what came before. But as workflows become empowered by AI, teams run into the same question: how do we make this automation production-ready?

item.title: Scorecards 2.0: Why we took scorecards further
item.description: Port had scorecards before. They helped you measure standards, but you couldn't act on them - no automations, no clear ownership, no permissions. Scorecards 2.0 rebuilds them as native catalog entities so you can define standards, track results, and fix issues in one place.

item.title: Finding engineering bottlenecks in Slack: a new way to measure developer experience
item.description: Developer metrics tell you what changed, but the day-to-day pain can be found in conversations. Zohar shares a prompt that turns Slack into a real-time DevEx sensor and the engineering friction patterns it uncovered at Port.

item.title: Port’s View as feature lets org admins see the product through any user’s permissions to reproduce issues, validate RBAC, and troubleshoot securely.
item.description: With View as, Port admins can instantly see the platform through any user’s permissions to validate access, debug RBAC issues, and troubleshoot confidently - securely and without impersonation.

item.title: What tens of thousands of AI prompts reveal about engineering teams
item.description: 10 months ago, we started releasing AI features in Port. Since then, AI has become an essential part of how teams work in Port. As you can see, AI adoption in Port organizations has taken off.

item.title: Why we made our product roadmap public
item.description: Port's product roadmap is publicly available to anyone who wants to see it. I wrote about why we did it and how our community has shaped Port through it.

item.title: Your Engineering Intelligence Tool Told you what’s broken. Now what?
item.description: Your Engineering Intelligence tool has metrics. What it's missing is the action that makes those metrics useful.

item.description: How Port's AI agents turn everyday support data into insights for every team

item.title: How we would have managed a recent incident at Port with an incident agent
item.description: ‍We had a real incident where three teams investigated the same problem in parallel. Here's what happened, what we built to make sure it doesn't happen again, and how we're using Port to move toward autonomous incident resolution.
